title: Under the Lights: BYU vs. Utah Men's Soccer
body:
On September 18, I photographed BYU and Utah men's soccer at BYU's South Field in Provo. It was my first night game, and it taught me more than any daytime shoot so far.

## Why this game

Before this game, most of my portfolio came from professional ultimate frisbee at golden hour, where the light does half the work for you. I wanted to prove I could deliver sharp, clean photos without the sun. A BYU and Utah rivalry match under stadium lights was the perfect test, with fast play, packed stands, and two teams whose colors look great on camera.

## Shooting under stadium lights

Night games force you to make trade-offs. To freeze players mid-tackle, I kept my shutter speed fast and my aperture wide, then let the ISO rise as high as it needed to go. The photos have more grain than my daytime work, but the action is sharp, and that matters more. I shot on my Sony a6700 with continuous autofocus and tracking, which kept up even when players crossed in front of each other.

![BYU number 27 rises above the pack for a header](/img/byu-vs-utah-05.jpg)

## The selective color edits

After the game, I wanted a few photos that felt different from a standard game gallery. I chose four frames where the BYU kit was clear and close to the camera, then edited them in Lightroom. I converted everything to black and white except the blue, then pushed the blue's saturation and brightness so the kits pop against the gray field. Last, I lifted the whites on the jerseys so the stripes stay crisp.

The result keeps attention on BYU's players, which makes these edits a good fit for team social media, posters, or a player's recruiting profile.

![Black and white with BYU blue: number 5 eyes the ball](/img/byu-vs-utah-bw-04.jpg)

## What I'm taking into the next game

- Arrive early and check where the light is strongest before warmups start.
- Trust high ISO. A sharp, grainy photo beats a clean, blurry one.
- Plan a few creative edits before the game, so I know which moments to look for.

You can see the full gallery from this game on the [home page](#home). If your team has a night game coming up, [send me the details](#book).
